headline.purpose: Landing section headings; console page title at 44px.

title.purpose: Stage titles, outcome titles, console ticket name.

title-sm.purpose: Door names, endpoint names, decision banner, scenario rows (20-26px).

body.purpose: Section intros and the hero subhead, max 56-64ch.

label.purpose: Buttons, nav, field names, gate names.

data.purpose: Endpoint paths, probabilities, credits, indexes, code, raw JSON. Never labels or headings.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Selected chips and tickets, primary buttons, travelling ticket, endpoint-card hover.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The one focus treatment for every interactive element.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions, door seals, ticket travel, reveals.

motion.name: tap
motion.value: 0.18s ease-out on border-color, box-shadow, transform, background-color
motion.purpose: Hover and press on interactive plates; press nudges 1px.

motion.name: door-seal
motion.purpose: Hazard panel dropping over a sealed door.

motion.name: ticket-travel
motion.purpose: The hero ticket moving door to door; the single authored motion moment.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: opacity 0, translateY 8px, blur 2px to rest, 0.45s ease-out
motion.purpose: Console gate rows arriving on the board.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0, translateY 14px to rest, 0.6s ease-out, staggered 90ms
motion.purpose: Endpoint cards on the landing only.

motion.name: chip-gestures
motion.value: scan 1.1s, blink 0.9s, nudge 0.8s, tilt 0.9s, drop 0.5s; once on hover or when live

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: durations 0.01ms, reveals at rest, airlock resolves instantly

narrative.overview:
Airlock is clean-room safety signage on clinical white. Every surface is a plate in a controlled room: white ground, hairline-bordered panels, solid signal colours that mean exactly one thing each. A ticket travels through sealed chambers and each Clocked verdict decides whether the next door opens; the visual system exists to make those verdicts legible at a glance, the way a door sign is legible from across a corridor.

Density is moderate and work-ready. The landing (Persuade) and the console (Operate) share one token set, one icon registry and one chip vocabulary; the console is denser and quieter, the landing larger and more staged. Colour is functional, never ornamental: red is safety, amber is core understanding, cyan is knowledge, green is clear. Condensed signage lettering carries headings; Geist carries everything you read; Geist Mono carries only what a machine produced.

Motion is short, eased out and tied to state. The hero's airlock run is the single authored motion moment; everything else is a settle, a hover, or a chip that plays once when its gate goes live.
keyCharacteristics: White ground across the whole product; depth from hairlines and soft shadows, not tinted backgrounds.
Three group signal colours with stable meanings, each in ink, fill, soft and line values.
Hazard stripes as the one loud device, reserved for sealed, locked and held states.
Lucide icons inside animated icon chips; no emoji, no glyph icons.
Barlow Condensed display over Geist UI, with Geist Mono for data only.

rules.name: The Ink-For-Text Rule
rules.body: Any colour that carries text or an icon uses its ink value (each at least 4.5:1 on white). Fills are for surfaces and graphics. Solid knowledge plates use knowledge-ink, never the bright knowledge-fill; solid core plates carry ink text, never white.

rules.name: The One-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Red is safety and blocking, amber is core and holding, cyan is knowledge, green is clear. A signal colour never appears as decoration or as a generic accent.

rules.name: The Hazard Rule
rules.body: Hazard stripes appear only on a sealed, locked or held state: the sealing panel over a sealed door, the band atop a locked or held decision banner, the swatch on a blocked or held verdict stamp. Never as decoration, dividers or section dressing.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for data, paths, probabilities and code only. Labels, headings and captions are Geist or Barlow, never mono.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No small uppercase label above a heading; group identity rides on colour, the plate band, or the heading's own numeral.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-State Rule
rules.body: A plate moves from Rest to Lift only when it is selected, hovered or the primary action. Stage belongs to the one hero object.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. No coloured side borders above 1px on cards; a quote well may carry a 1px neutral left rule.

dos: Do use each group colour's ink (#c8253a, #8f5f00, #067782) for any text or icon; keep it at 4.5:1 or better on white.
Do put solid knowledge plates on #067782, not #0aa5b2, wherever they carry text or icons.
Do reserve hazard stripes for sealed, locked and held states.
Do keep the hero airlock run the single authored motion moment; scroll reveal is limited to the endpoint grid.
Do use Geist Mono only for data, paths, probabilities and code, with tabular slashed-zero numerals.
Do give every endpoint its Lucide icon inside an animated icon chip.
Do honour reduced motion: the airlock resolves instantly and reveals show at rest.
donts: Don't put white text or icons on the bright cyan (#0aa5b2) or amber (#f2a900) fills.
Don't use hazard stripes as decoration, dividers or section dressing.
Don't add scroll reveal to hero, scenario or closing sections.
Don't set labels, captions or headings in mono.
Don't place eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't use coloured side borders above 1px on cards.
Don't use emoji or glyph icons; use Lucide inside icon chips.
Don't tint the ground; the product stays on white.
